key_insight: MICViT improves 3D brain MRI prediction by separately modeling modality-specific and cross-modal information at both local and global scales.
clinical_relevance: Better use of multiple MRI sequences could improve robustness and accuracy in neuroimaging tasks such as brain age estimation and potentially broader multimodal brain analysis.
method: Four attention paths: intra-modal local/global and cross-modal local/global
Learns interactions across co-registered sequences such as T1, FLAIR, DWI, and SWI
evidence_signal: Evaluated on brain age prediction across UK Biobank (n=41,404), SOOP (n=1,062), and Cam-CAN (n=613), where MICViT outperformed CNN and transformer baselines and gained more from adding modalities.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown for brain age prediction, so broader clinical utility and generalization to other MRI tasks still need validation.
paper_title: Modeling Local, Global, and Cross-Modal Context in Multimodal 3D MRI
